gist: Opens the chapter 'The Six Keys of Eudoxus', a first-person practical text covering the First Key (freeing the Sulphur/seed and the first purification of the Stone to whiteness), the Second Key (philosophical sublimation and gentle dissolution of the Stone by the unrevealed Secret Fire, ending in putrefaction) and the long Third Key (preparation of 'our Mercury' by dissolving the body, keeping the black residue, washing the earth repeatedly with its own water to extract the Fixed Salt, and reuniting soul, spirit and body), then distinguishes the compound of Nature from the compound of Art and names the thickening Pontick Water. No Atwood commentary appears; the chunk breaks off mid-passage.

notes.point: Chapter heading: 'The Six Keys of Eudoxus, Opening Into the Most Secret Philosophy'. The body is spoken by a first-person 'I' addressing 'you' / 'the true Sons of Science'; by the heading this is Eudoxus. Atwood does not speak in her own voice, nor state endorsement, in this chunk.

The First Key opens the dark prisons in which the Sulphur is shut up; it extracts the seed out of the body and forms the Stone of the philosophers by conjoining spirit with body, i.e. sulphur with mercury.

Hermes is cited as demonstrating the First Key: in the caverns of the metals is hidden the Stone, venerable, bright in colour, a sublime mind and an open sea; it contains a Spirit of sublime origin and is the Sea of the Wise, in which they angle for their mysterious Fish.

The operations of the three works are much alike, and the philosophers deliberately speak equivocally so that those without 'the Lynx's eyes' go wrong and are lost in the labyrinth; when they seem to speak of one work they often treat of another.

In each work the Artist must dissolve the body with the spirit, cut off the Raven's head, whiten the Black and vivify the White; but it is properly in the First operation that he cuts off the head of the Black Dragon and the Raven. Hence Hermes: 'What is born of the Crow is the beginning of this Art.'

By separating the black, foul, stinking fume of the Blackest Black, the astral, white, resplendent Stone is formed, which holds in its veins the blood of the Pelican. The First Key ends at this First Purification and shining whiteness.
The Second Key dissolves the compound of the Stone and begins the philosophical separation of the Elements, done only by raising the subtle and pure parts above the thick and terrestrial.

Whoever can sublime the Stone philosophically deserves the name philosopher, because he knows the Fire of the Wise, the only instrument of this sublimation. No philosopher has openly revealed this Secret Fire, the powerful agent of all the Art's wonders.

One who cannot understand the Fire or distinguish it by the characters used to describe it should stop and pray: its knowledge is more a gift of Heaven than a light of natural reasoning. Still he should read the philosophers, meditate and above all pray; every difficulty yields at last to Work, Meditation and Prayer.

Without sublimation, the conversion of the Elements and extraction of the Principles is impossible; this conversion (Water of Earth, Air of Water, Fire of Air) is the only way to prepare 'our Mercury'.

The Secret Fire dissolves the Stone naturally and without violence into Water in the great sea of the Wise, by a distillation made by the rays of the Sun and Moon. Thus the Stone, 'the vine of the Wise' according to Hermes, becomes their Wine, which by Art yields their rectified Water of Life and most sharp Vinegar.

The Stone's Elements can be dissolved only by 'this Nature wholly Divine', and perfect dissolution comes only after a proportioned digestion and putrefaction, where the Second Key 'of the First Work' ends.

The Third Key contains a longer train of operations than all the others together. Because the Perfection of 'our Mercury' depends on it, philosophers say little; even the sincerest (Artefius, Trevisan, Flammel) passed over the Preparation of our Mercury in silence, and nearly all feigned instead of showing this longest and most important operation.

The speaker promises to enlarge on it more than others, or at least set in order what they treated confusedly; without the inspiration of Heaven or the help of a faithful friend one stays lost in this labyrinth.

The Third Key's intention: separation and purification of the Principles of our Mercury, by perfect dissolution and glorification of the body from which it was born, and by intimate union of the soul with its body, the Spirit being the only tie of this conjunction. It ends in a new substance infinitely nobler than the first.

After the spring of living water has been drawn from the stone and the vine pressed into wine, the Artist must note that this apparently homogeneous water contains three substances and principles, Salt, Sulphur and Mercury, which are spirit, soul and body; they seem united but are far from it. When the Water (soul and spirit) is distilled off, the Body stays at the bottom like dead, black, dredgy earth, which is not to be despised, since nothing in 'our subject' is not good.

John Pontanus holds that the Stone's very superfluities become a true essence, that whoever separates anything from the subject knows nothing of philosophy, and that the whole compound, dregs included, is perfected by 'our Fire'. This corrects those who think purification means taking the subtile and casting away the heavy.
notes.voice: QUOTED: John Pontanus (cited by Eudoxus, endorsed)

notes.point: Hermes: its power is not integral until turned into earth. Fire and Sulphur are hidden in the centre of the Earth, which must be washed exactly with its own spirit to extract the Fixed Salt, the Blood of our Stone. This is the essential Mystery, completed only after convenient digestion and slow distillation.

Fire and water are contrary, yet the Artist must make peace between these enemies who radically love each other. Cosmopolite: being purged, they make Fire and Water friends in their earth which ascended with them. Hence: moisten the earth often with its water.

The body must be dissolved by the water and the Earth penetrated with its Humidity to be fit for generation. Per the philosophers, the Spirit is Eve and the Body Adam, to be joined for propagation; Hermes: Water is the strongest Nature, which surmounts and excites the fixed Nature in the Body, 'that is, rejoices in it'.

The two substances, same nature but different genders, ascend together insensibly, leaving little faeces; soul, spirit and body finally appear inseparably united in a nobler Form, as different from the first liquid form as exactly rectified alcohol of Wine 'actuated with its salt' differs from wine. This comparison is said to give precise knowledge of the Third Key.
'Our Water' is a living Spring issuing from the Stone by a natural miracle; Hermes says the water issuing from the Stone is first of all and the foundation of the Art.

Philosophers call this water wine, water of life, vinegar or oil according to its degree of Preparation or its effects; it is properly the Vinegar of the Wise. Its distillation behaves like common vinegar: water and phlegm rise first, the oily substance, in which the water's efficacy lies, comes last.

Therefore the body must be dissolved entirely to extract all its humidity, which contains the precious ferment, the sulphur, balm of Nature and wonderful unguent; without it the blackness desired by all philosophers will never appear in the vessel.

Reduce the whole compound into water and perfectly unite volatile with fixed. Senior's precept: the highest fume is to be reduced to the lowest, for the divine water descends from heaven and reduces the soul to its body, which it at length revives.

The Balm of Life is hidden in the unclean faeces; wash them with the celestial water until their blackness is removed, and the Water will then be animated with the Fiery Essence that works all the Art's wonders.

Philosophers have two compounds. The compound of Nature (spoken of in the First Key) is made by Nature in a way incomprehensible to the Artist, who only lends Nature a hand by applying external things. The compound of Art is made by the Wise man through the secret union of fixed with volatile, with a prudence gained only from profound philosophy; it differs somewhat in the Second and Third Work but is always the Artist's making.
Geber defines the compound as a mixture of Argent vive and Sulphur, i.e. volatile and fixed, which act on one another and are reciprocally volatilized and fixed into perfect Fixity.
Nature's example: earth bears no fruit unless penetrated by its humidity, and humidity stays barren unless retained and fixed by the dryness of earth.

So in the Art: in the first work one must purify the Serpent born of the Slime of the earth and whiten the foul black faeces to separate the white sulphur, the Sal Amoniac of the Wise and their Chaste Diana bathing; the whole mystery is but the extraction of the fixed salt of the compound, in which all the energy of our Mercury consists.

Water rising by distillation carries up part of this fiery salt, so affusion of the water on the body, reiterated many times, impregnates, fattens and fertilizes our Mercury and makes it fit to be fixed, which is the end of the second Work. Hermes: seeing the water grow by degrees thicker and harder, he rejoiced, knowing he would find what he sought.

This viscous liquor is rightly called Pontick Water: its exuberant ponticity is the true mark of its virtue, which grows the more it is rectified and worked. It is called Water of Life because it gives life to the metals, but properly the great Lunaria for its shining brightness. The text breaks off with '....'.

method.veiled: opens the dark prisons in which the Sulphur is shut up
method.plain: The active principle (Sulphur) is locked inside the body; the First Key releases it, which the same sentence calls extracting 'the seed out of the body'.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3: the same sentence glosses the First Key as that which 'knows how to extract the seed out of the body'.

method.veiled: forms the Stone of the philosophers by the conjunction of the spirit with the body -- of sulphur with mercury
method.plain: The Stone is first formed by joining spirit and body; 'sulphur with mercury' is given in apposition as another name for the same joining.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3, the dash sets the two pairs in apposition. Whether sulphur pairs with spirit and mercury with body is only positional (see ambiguities).

method.veiled: In the caverns of the metals there is hidden the Stone, which is venerable, bright in colour, a mind sublime, and an open sea
method.plain: The Stone lies hidden within 'the metals' and must be uncovered; it is bright, contains a spirit of sublime origin, and is a 'sea' in which the wise seek their 'Fish'.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3: cited as Hermes' demonstration of the First Key; restated as 'it contains a Spirit of a sublime original; it is the Sea of the Wise'. What 'the metals' are is not stated (see ambiguities).

method.veiled: the philosophers do designedly speak in equivocal terms, to the end that those who have not the Lynx's eyes may pursue wrong
method.plain: Authors deliberately blur which of three analogous works they describe; the reader-operator must sharply discriminate which work is meant.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3: 'when one imagines that they speak of one work, they often treat of another'.

method.veiled: in each work the Wise Artist ought to dissolve the body with the spirit
method.plain: In every work the body is dissolved by means of the spirit.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3, said to hold 'in each work'.

method.veiled: he must cut off the Raven's head, whiten the Black, and vivify the White
method.plain: A recurring sequence in each work: end the black stage, bring the matter to whiteness, then give life to the white.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3: listed as what happens 'in each work'; the paragraph ends with separation of the black fume yielding the white Stone at 'this shining whiteness'.

method.veiled: it is properly in the First operation that the Wise Artist cuts off the head of the Black Dragon and of the Raven
method.plain: Removal of the blackness belongs chiefly to the first operation.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3: followed by 'What is born of the Crow is the beginning of this Art' and by the separation of the 'Blackest Black' that ends the First Key.

method.veiled: What is born of the Crow is the beginning of this Art
method.plain: The Art begins from what comes out of the black stage.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3: introduced with 'Hence' after the Raven/Black Dragon passage; the white Stone is formed by separating the black fume.

method.veiled: it is by separation of the black, foul, and stinking fume of the Blackest Black that our astral, white, and resplendent Stone is formed
method.plain: Separating off a black, foul vapour leaves a pure, white, shining Stone.

method.veiled: It is at this First Purification of the Stone, and at this shining whiteness, that the work of the First Key is ended
method.plain: Shining whiteness marks the end of the First Key.

method.veiled: which contains in its veins the blood of the Pelican
method.plain: The white Stone holds an inner vital content; the text does not say what 'blood of the Pelican' is.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3 only; compare 'the Fixed Salt, which is the Blood of our Stone' (IV.3 ¶7). See ambiguities.

method.veiled: this separation of the elements is not made but by raising up the subtle and pure parts above the thick and terrestrial parts
method.plain: The Second Key separates the elements by sublimation: lifting the fine, pure part above the coarse, earthy part.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶5 defines the separation this way; the next sentence calls it to 'sublime the Stone philosophically'.

method.veiled: the Fire of the Wise, which is the only instrument which can work this sublimation
method.plain: A special 'fire', never openly named, is the sole agent of the sublimation; the text gives its functions (dissolves the Stone naturally, without violence, into water; perfects the whole compound) but withholds its identity.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶5: 'No philosopher has ever openly revealed this Secret Fire'; 'this Secret Fire, which dissolves the Stone naturally and without violence'. IV.3 ¶7: whole compound 'made perfect by the action of our Fire'.

method.veiled: the knowledge of this great Secret is rather a gift of Heaven, than a Light acquired by the natural force of reasoning
method.plain: One who cannot recognize the Fire by its described characters should stop and seek it by prayer, reading the philosophers and meditation; its knowledge comes more by illumination than by reasoning.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶5: 'there is no difficulty which may not in the end be made clear by Work, Meditation, and Prayer'.

method.veiled: this conversion, which makes Water of Earth, Air of Water, and Fire of Air, is the only way whereby our Mercury can be prepared
method.plain: Preparing 'our Mercury' requires a stepwise upward conversion of the elements, which in turn requires the sublimation.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶5: 'Without the sublimation of the Stone, the conversion of the Elements and the extraction of the Principles is impossible'.

method.veiled: makes it dissolve into Water in the great sea of the Wise, by the distillation which is made by the rays of the Sun and Moon
method.plain: The Secret Fire dissolves the Stone into a water through a distillation ascribed to 'the rays of the Sun and Moon'; whether literal or figurative is not stated.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶5 only; see ambiguities.

method.veiled: the Stone, which, according to Hermes, is the vine of the Wise, becomes their Wine, which, by the operations of Art, produces their rectified Water of Life, and their most sharp Vinegar
method.plain: The dissolved Stone yields a liquid ('Wine'), which further work refines into 'Water of Life' and 'Vinegar'.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶5 ('It is in this manner' refers back to the dissolution into Water); IV.3 ¶8 says such names mark degrees of preparation or effects of one water.

method.veiled: this Nature wholly Divine
method.plain: The only thing that can dissolve the Stone's Elements; in context, the Secret Fire.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶5: the Secret Fire 'dissolves the Stone', and a few lines later the Elements 'cannot be dissolved but by this Nature wholly Divine'; the identity is implied by 'this', not asserted.

method.veiled: nor can a perfect dissolution be made of it, but after a proportioned digestion and putrefaction, at which the operation of the Second Key of the First Work is ended
method.plain: Full dissolution needs a measured period of digestion and putrefaction; this closes the Second Key.

method.veiled: there is hardly one found who has not feigned, instead of showing the longest and the most important of the operations of our Practice
method.plain: The Preparation of our Mercury (Third Key), the longest and most important operation, is passed over or feigned by the authors, even the sincerest.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7: 'the sincerest even, as Artefius, Trevisan, Flammel, have passed in silence the Preparation of our Mercury'.

method.veiled: without the inspiration of Heaven, or without the help of a faithful friend, one remains undoubtedly in this labyrinth
method.plain: Because the books treat the Third Key confusedly, the operator needs divine inspiration or a trustworthy guide.

method.veiled: a perfect dissolution and glorification of the body, whence it had its nativity, and by the intimate union of the soul with its body, of whom the Spirit is the only tie which works this conjunction
method.plain: The Third Key separates and purifies the Principles of Mercury by fully dissolving and exalting the original body, then reunites soul with body through the spirit as sole link.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7: 'This is the Intention, and the essential point of the Operations of this Key'.

method.veiled: the generation of a new substance infinitely nobler than the First
method.plain: The Third Key ends in a new, far nobler substance.

method.veiled: After the Wise Artist has made a spring of living water come out of the stone, and has pressed out the vine of the philosophers, and has made their wine
method.plain: Starting point of the Third Key's work: the Stone has already been dissolved into its water/'wine' (the Second Key's result).
method.basis: IV.3 ¶5 describes the Stone ('vine of the Wise') becoming 'their Wine' by dissolution; IV.3 ¶7 opens with 'After' these steps.

method.veiled: in this homogeneous substance, which appears under the form of Water, there are three different substances, and three natural principles of bodies --- Salt, Sulphur and Mercury --- which are the spirit, the soul, and the body
method.plain: The water obtained looks uniform but holds three principles that are not yet truly united and must be separated, purified and reunited.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7: 'though they appear pure and perfectly united together, there still wants much of their being so'. One-to-one pairing is ambiguous (see ambiguities).

method.veiled: when by distillation we draw the Water, which is the soul and the spirit, the Body remains in the bottom of the vessel, like a dead, black, and dredgy earth
method.plain: Distilling off the water (soul and spirit) leaves a black residue (the body), which must be kept, not discarded.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7: 'which, nevertheless, is not to be despised; for in our subject there is nothing which is not good'; Pontanus: 'he who pretends to separate anything from our subject knows nothing of philosophy'.

method.veiled: persuade themselves that they must only take the subtile and cast away the heavy
method.plain: Error: thinking purification means keeping only the fine part; the whole compound, dregs included, is perfected by 'our Fire'.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7: 'the whole compound, is made perfect by the action of our Fire'.

method.veiled: power of it is not integral until it be turned into earth
method.plain: The matter reaches its full power only once brought into an earthy (fixed) state.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7: given with 'But' against discarding the heavy part, and followed by Fire and Sulphur being hidden 'in the centre of the Earth'. The referent of 'it' is not specified.

method.veiled: the Fire and the Sulphur are hidden in the centre of the Earth
method.plain: The active principles lie inside the residual earth, which is why it must not be thrown away but washed.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7: the 'Earth' here follows the description of the Body remaining 'like a dead, black, and dredgy earth', and is to be washed 'with its spirit'.

method.veiled: they must wash it exactly with its spirit, to extract out of it the Fixed Salt, which is the Blood of our Stone
method.plain: The residual earth is washed with its own distilled spirit to draw out its fixed salt; completed only through convenient digestion and slow distillation.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7: 'This is the essential Mystery of the operation, which is not accomplished till after a convenient digestion and a slow distillation'.

method.veiled: the Wise Artist must make peace between the enemies, who radically love each other vehemently
method.plain: The contraries fire and water must be reconciled; per Cosmopolite this happens, once they are purged, in their own earth that ascended with them.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7: 'Cosmopolite told the manner thereof'; immediately followed by 'moisten oftentimes the earth with its water'.

method.veiled: moisten oftentimes the earth with its water, and you will obtain what you seek
method.plain: Repeatedly pour the distilled water back on its own residue.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7; IV.3 ¶9 repeats: 'the affusion of the water on the body, reiterated many times'.

method.veiled: the Spirit is Eve, the Body is Adam; they ought to be joined together for the propagation of their species
method.plain: Spirit and body are a female/male pair that must be united for 'generation'; the body must first be dissolved by the water and the earth penetrated with its humidity.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7: 'Must not the body be dissolved by the water, and the Earth be penetrated with its Humidity, to be made proper for generation?'; 'two substances, which are of the same nature but of different genders'.

method.veiled: Water is the strongest Nature which surmounts and excites the fixed Nature in the Body, that is, rejoices in it
method.plain: The water acts on and enlivens the fixed part held in the body.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7, offered as Hermes saying 'the same' as the Eve/Adam union.

method.veiled: ascend insensibly together, leaving but a little faeces in the bottom of their vessel
method.plain: Sign of success in the Third Key: spirit and body rise together leaving little residue.

method.veiled: as different from its first liquid Form as the alcohol of Wine exactly rectified and actuated with its salt is different from the substance of the wine
method.plain: The reunited soul, spirit and body are to the first liquid what rectified spirit of wine charged with its own salt is to plain wine.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7 calls the comparison 'very fitting' and a 'precise knowledge of the operations of the Third Key'.

method.veiled: Our Water is a living Spring which comes out of the Stone by a natural miracle of our philosophy
method.plain: The key liquid is drawn from the Stone itself; it is the foundation of the Art and is properly the 'Vinegar of the Wise'.

method.veiled: according to the different degrees of Preparation, or according to the diverse effects which it is capable of producing
method.plain: The many names of the water (wine, water of life, vinegar, oil) mark its stage of preparation or its effect, not different substances.

method.veiled: the water and the phlegm ascend first; the oily substance, in which the efficacy of the water consists, comes the last
method.plain: In distilling this liquor, as with common vinegar, the watery part comes first and the effective oily part last; so the body must be wholly dissolved to get all of it.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶8: 'It is therefore necessary to dissolve the body entirely'.

method.veiled: this blackness so desired by all the philosophers
method.plain: A desired blackness in the vessel appears only if the body is wholly dissolved and all its humidity (the ferment, sulphur, balm) extracted.

method.veiled: Reduce then the whole compound into water, and make a perfect union of the volatile with the fixed
method.plain: Dissolve everything into water and unite the volatile with the fixed.

method.veiled: the highest fume should be reduced to the lowest
method.plain: What has risen as vapour is to be brought back down onto what remains below, uniting volatile with fixed.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶8: given as Senior's precept right after 'make a perfect union of the volatile with the fixed', and explained by the water as 'the reducer of the soul to its body'.

method.veiled: the divine water is the thing descending from heaven, the reducer of the soul to its body, which it at length revives
method.plain: The water, returned onto the body, carries the soul back to it and finally revives it.

method.veiled: you ought to wash them with this celestial water until you have removed away the blackness from them
method.plain: Wash the black dregs with the water until they lose their blackness; the water then becomes charged with the 'Fiery Essence'.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶8: 'The Balm of Life is hid in these unclean faeces'; 'then your Water shall be animated with this Fiery Essence'.

method.veiled: who does nothing but lend a hand to Nature by the adhibition of external things
method.plain: For the compound of Nature (First Key) the Artist only assists Nature by applying external means; Nature produces it.

method.veiled: the secret union of the fixed with the volatile, perfectly conjoined with all prudence, which cannot be acquired but by the lights of a profound philosophy
method.plain: The compound of Art is made by the Artist himself by uniting fixed and volatile, which requires profound philosophical understanding.

method.veiled: which, acting on one another, are volatilized and fixed reciprocally into a perfect Fixity
method.plain: Volatile and fixed act on each other until both reach a stable fixed state; illustrated by earth and its moisture needing each other to bear fruit.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶9: Geber's definition and the 'example of Nature'.

method.veiled: purify the Serpent, born of the Slime of the earth
method.plain: A first-work task, paired with whitening the black faeces; what the Serpent denotes is not stated.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶9 only; followed by 'all this mystery is but the extraction of the fixed salt of our compound'.

method.veiled: the white sulphur, which is the Sal Amoniac of the Wise, and their Chaste Diana, who washes herself in the bath
method.plain: Whitening the black faeces separates a white sulphur; the whole 'mystery' is the extraction of the fixed salt of the compound.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶9: 'all this mystery is but the extraction of the fixed salt of our compound, in which the whole energy of our Mercury consists'.

method.veiled: the affusion of the water on the body, reiterated many times, impregnates, fattens, and fertilizes our Mercury, and makes it fit to be fixed
method.plain: Distilled water carries up part of the fiery salt; pouring it back on the body many times enriches the Mercury until it can be fixed (end of the second Work).
method.basis: IV.3 ¶9: 'The water which ascends by distillation carries up with it a part of this fiery salt'.

method.veiled: the water by degrees did become thicker and harder
method.plain: Progressive thickening of the water shows the work is succeeding.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶9: 'I certainly knew that I should find what I sought for'.

method.veiled: Its exuberant ponticity is indeed the true character of its virtue
method.plain: The viscous liquor's ponticity marks its strength, which increases with rectification and working.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶9: 'the more you shall rectify it, and the more you shall work upon it, the more virtue will it acquire'.

terms.meaning: One of six named stages of operation. The First ends at the first purification and whiteness of the Stone; the Second (sublimation and dissolution) at digestion and putrefaction; the Third, the longest, is the preparation of our Mercury, ending in a new nobler substance from reunited principles.

quotes.text: The Third Key comprehends of itself alone a longer train of operations than all the rest together.

terms.meaning: Three works with analogous operations which philosophers deliberately confuse. How they map onto the Keys is not consistent within the chunk (see ambiguities).

quotes.text: the operations of the three works have a great deal of analogy one to another
makes it fit to be fixed, which is the end of the second Work

terms.meaning: Formed in the First Key by conjunction of spirit with body and by separating off the black fume; hidden in the caverns of the metals; sublimed and dissolved in the Second Key; the source from which 'our Water' springs.

equivalences.quote: it is the Sea of the Wise, in which they angle for their mysterious Fish
the Stone, which, according to Hermes, is the vine of the Wise

quotes.text: forms the Stone of the philosophers by the conjunction of the spirit with the body
our astral, white, and resplendent Stone is formed, which contains in its veins the blood of the Pelican

terms.meaning: Hermes' name for the Stone, in which the wise angle for their Fish; also where the Stone is dissolved into Water.

equivalences.quote: This Stone has a bright glittering: it contains a Spirit of a sublime original; it is the Sea of the Wise

quotes.text: makes it dissolve into Water in the great sea of the Wise

terms.meaning: Shut up in 'dark prisons' and freed by the First Key; paired with mercury in the conjunction that forms the Stone; one of the three principles; contained in the body's humidity as the precious ferment; hidden with the Fire in the centre of the Earth. The white sulphur is separated by whitening the black faeces.

equivalences.with: precious ferment / balm of Nature / wonderful unguent
equivalences.quote: the precious ferment, the sulphur, that balm of Nature, and wonderful unguent

equivalences.with: Sal Amoniac of the Wise / Chaste Diana (white sulphur)
equivalences.quote: the white sulphur, which is the Sal Amoniac of the Wise, and their Chaste Diana, who washes herself in the bath

quotes.text: opens the dark prisons in which the Sulphur is shut up
the Fire and the Sulphur are hidden in the centre of the Earth

terms.meaning: What the Third Key prepares and perfects; prepared only through conversion of the Elements; its Principles are separated, purified and reunited; its whole energy lies in the fixed salt; impregnated by repeated affusion until fit to be fixed. Also named as one of the three principles and paired with sulphur in the First Key's conjunction.

quotes.text: this conversion, which makes Water of Earth, Air of Water, and Fire of Air, is the only way whereby our Mercury can be prepared
the extraction of the fixed salt of our compound, in which the whole energy of our Mercury consists

terms.meaning: The unrevealed agent of the Art, the only instrument of philosophical sublimation; dissolves the Stone naturally and without violence into water; perfects the whole compound, dregs included. By context apparently also 'this Nature wholly Divine' (¶5). Its identity is not given.

equivalences.quote: the Fire of the Wise, which is the only instrument which can work this sublimation. No philosopher has ever openly revealed this Secret Fire

quotes.text: this Secret Fire, which dissolves the Stone naturally and without violence
The Elements of the Stone cannot be dissolved but by this Nature wholly Divine

terms.meaning: Raising the subtle and pure parts above the thick and terrestrial; effected only by the Fire of the Wise; prerequisite for converting the Elements and extracting the Principles.

quotes.text: this separation of the elements is not made but by raising up the subtle and pure parts above the thick and terrestrial parts
Without the sublimation of the Stone, the conversion of the Elements and the extraction of the Principles is impossible

terms.meaning: Earth, Water, Air, Fire: separated philosophically in the Second Key and converted in sequence upward in preparing Mercury.

quotes.text: makes Water of Earth, Air of Water, and Fire of Air

terms.meaning: Three principles in the apparently homogeneous water: Salt, Sulphur and Mercury, also called spirit, soul and body. They seem united but must be separated, purified and reunited.

equivalences.quote: Salt, Sulphur and Mercury --- which are the spirit, the soul, and the body

quotes.text: though they appear pure and perfectly united together, there still wants much of their being so

terms.meaning: The three components of the matter. The distilled Water is soul and spirit; the Body is the residue. Spirit is the only tie uniting soul with body. Spirit and Body are female and male (Eve and Adam), of the same nature but different genders.

equivalences.quote: we draw the Water, which is the soul and the spirit, the Body remains in the bottom of the vessel
the Spirit is Eve, the Body is Adam

quotes.text: of whom the Spirit is the only tie which works this conjunction
these two substances, which are of the same nature but of different genders

terms.meaning: The residual body left after the water is distilled off; holds Fire and Sulphur in its centre; to be washed and moistened often with its own water/spirit, not discarded; where fire and water are reconciled.

equivalences.quote: the Body remains in the bottom of the vessel, like a dead, black, and dredgy earth

quotes.text: moisten oftentimes the earth with its water, and you will obtain what you seek

terms.meaning: Extracted from the residual earth by washing it with its own spirit; holds all the energy of our Mercury; partly carried up by the distilling water. ¶9 presents separating the white sulphur from the faeces as 'but the extraction of the fixed salt'.

equivalences.quote: the Fixed Salt, which is the Blood of our Stone

quotes.text: all this mystery is but the extraction of the fixed salt of our compound
The water which ascends by distillation carries up with it a part of this fiery salt

terms.meaning: The living spring drawn from the Stone, the foundation of the Art; its names vary with degree of preparation or effect; properly the Vinegar of the Wise. Descends from heaven and reduces the soul to its body; animated by the Fiery Essence; carrying up the fiery salt it grows viscous ('Pontick'); called Water of Life as giving life to the metals, properly the great Lunaria for its brightness.

equivalences.with: wine / water of life / vinegar / oil
equivalences.quote: sometimes they call it wine, sometimes water of life, sometimes vinegar, sometimes oil
it is properly called the Vinegar of the Wise
the philosophers give this viscous Liquor the name of Pontick Water
It has been called the Water of Life, because it gives life to the metals; but it is properly called the great Lunaria

quotes.text: Our Water is a living Spring which comes out of the Stone by a natural miracle of our philosophy.
the divine water is the thing descending from heaven, the reducer of the soul to its body, which it at length revives

terms.meaning: A quality of the viscous water that is the true mark of its virtue and grows with rectification and working. No further definition is given.

quotes.text: Its exuberant ponticity is indeed the true character of its virtue

terms.meaning: Images of the black stage or matter, whose 'head' is cut off chiefly in the first operation by separating the black, foul fume, from which the white Stone results; the Art begins from what is born of it.

quotes.text: cuts off the head of the Black Dragon and of the Raven
the black, foul, and stinking fume of the Blackest Black

variants: this blackness so desired by all the philosophers
terms.meaning: A desired appearance in the vessel, seen only if all the body's humidity (with its sulphur) is extracted; separately, the blackness of the faeces must be washed away.

quotes.text: without which you ought not to hope ever to see in your vessel this blackness so desired by all the philosophers

terms.meaning: Contained in the veins of the white Stone; not explained (see ambiguities).

quotes.text: which contains in its veins the blood of the Pelican

terms.meaning: Dregs or residue. Not to be discarded: the Stone's superfluities are converted into true essence, the Balm of Life is hidden in the faeces, and they are washed and whitened to separate the white sulphur / fixed salt. Little faeces remain when spirit and body rise united.

quotes.text: the very superfluities of the Stone are converted into a true essence
The Balm of Life is hid in these unclean faeces

terms.meaning: The vital principle hidden in the body's humidity and in the faeces; washed out into the Water, which is then 'animated with this Fiery Essence'. ¶8 equates the ferment/balm of Nature with the sulphur; the link Balm of Life = Fiery Essence is by sequence, not asserted.

equivalences.quote: the precious ferment, the sulphur, that balm of Nature, and wonderful unguent

quotes.text: then your Water shall be animated with this Fiery Essence, which works all the wonders of our Art

terms.meaning: Two kinds. The compound of Nature (First Key) is made by Nature, the Artist only assisting. The compound of Art is made by the Artist by secretly uniting fixed with volatile, and differs somewhat between the Second and Third Work. Per Geber, a mixture of Argent vive and Sulphur.

equivalences.with: mixture of Argent vive and Sulphur (volatile and fixed)
equivalences.quote: a mixture of Argent vive and Sulphur, that is to say, of the volatile and the fixed

quotes.text: the philosophers have two sorts of compounds

terms.meaning: The two components to be united. They act on each other and are reciprocally volatilized and fixed until perfectly fixed; in Geber's formula Argent vive corresponds to the volatile and Sulphur to the fixed (by order of the 'that is to say').

equivalences.quote: Argent vive and Sulphur, that is to say, of the volatile and the fixed

quotes.text: make a perfect union of the volatile with the fixed

terms.meaning: Named operations: perfect dissolution follows proportioned digestion and putrefaction (end of the Second Key); extraction of the Fixed Salt needs convenient digestion and slow distillation.

quotes.text: a proportioned digestion and putrefaction
not accomplished till after a convenient digestion and a slow distillation

variants: affusion of the water on the body
terms.meaning: Pouring the distilled water back onto the body, repeated many times, to impregnate the Mercury with the fiery salt.

quotes.text: the affusion of the water on the body, reiterated many times, impregnates, fattens, and fertilizes our Mercury

variants: Serpent, born of the Slime of the earth
terms.meaning: Something to be purified in the first work, alongside whitening the black faeces; not further defined.

quotes.text: purify the Serpent, born of the Slime of the earth

terms.meaning: The operator. One who can sublime the Stone 'justly deserves the name of a philosopher'.

quotes.text: He who knows how to sublime the Stone philosophically, justly deserves the name of a philosopher

sources.name: Eudoxus
sources.work: The Six Keys of Eudoxus, Opening Into the Most Secret Philosophy
sources.use: Named in the chapter heading as author of the Keys; the first-person speaker of the whole chunk.

sources.name: Hermes
sources.quote: In the caverns of the metals there is hidden the Stone, which is venerable, bright in colour, a mind sublime, and an open sea.
sources.use: Supports, cited repeatedly: demonstrates the First Key; 'What is born of the Crow is the beginning of this Art'; the Stone as 'vine of the Wise'; power 'not integral until it be turned into earth'; Water as strongest Nature exciting the fixed Nature in the Body; the water issuing from the Stone is first and the foundation of the Art; rejoicing as the water grew thicker and harder.

sources.name: Artefius
sources.use: Named with Trevisan and Flammel among 'the sincerest' who still passed the Preparation of our Mercury in silence.

sources.name: Trevisan
sources.use: As Artefius: silent on the Preparation of our Mercury.

sources.name: Flammel
sources.use: As Artefius: silent on the Preparation of our Mercury.

sources.name: John Pontanus
sources.use: Supports: the Stone's superfluities become a true essence; whoever separates anything from the subject knows nothing of philosophy; the whole compound is perfected by 'our Fire'. Used against discarding the heavy part.

sources.name: Cosmopolite
sources.quote: All things must therefore being purged make Fire and Water to be Friends, which they will easily do in their earth, which had ascended with them.
sources.use: Supports: the manner of reconciling fire and water in their own earth.

sources.name: philosophers
sources.quote: the Spirit is Eve, the Body is Adam
sources.use: Reported view supporting the union of spirit and body for generation.

sources.name: Senior
sources.quote: the highest fume should be reduced to the lowest
sources.use: Supports: precept for uniting volatile with fixed.

sources.name: Geber
sources.quote: a mixture of Argent vive and Sulphur
sources.use: Supports: definition of the compound of Art as volatile and fixed reciprocally fixed into perfect Fixity.

ambiguities.quote: Salt, Sulphur and Mercury --- which are the spirit, the soul, and the body
readings: Positional one-to-one mapping: Salt = spirit, Sulphur = soul, Mercury = body.
Only a collective identity: the three principles are the triad spirit/soul/body, with no pairing intended.
ambiguities.basis: The list order suggests the first reading, but the chunk's other positional pairings do not line up: ¶3 'the spirit with the body -- of sulphur with mercury' would put sulphur with spirit (not soul) and mercury with body; ¶9 'Argent vive and Sulphur, that is to say, of the volatile and the fixed' makes Sulphur the fixed. The Fixed Salt is extracted from the body/earth (¶7), which does not obviously fit Salt = spirit.

ambiguities.quote: at which the operation of the Second Key of the First Work is ended
readings: The Keys are sub-stages within the Works: the First and Second Keys belong to the First Work, and the 'second Work' ended in ¶9 corresponds to a later Key.

'Work' and 'Key' overlap inconsistently: ¶9 places purifying the Serpent and whitening the faeces 'in the first work' and the Mercury made 'fit to be fixed' at 'the end of the second Work', material that sits within the Third Key's discussion.
ambiguities.basis: ¶3 says the three works are analogous and deliberately confused; ¶5 'Second Key of the First Work'; ¶9 'in the first work', 'the end of the second Work', and 'not altogether the same in the Second as in the Third Work'.

ambiguities.quote: by the distillation which is made by the rays of the Sun and Moon
readings: Literal use of solar and lunar light or influence in the distillation.
Figurative expression for the action of the Secret Fire.
ambiguities.basis: The same paragraph says the Secret Fire is never openly revealed, dissolves 'naturally and without violence' and is 'this Nature wholly Divine'; nothing in the chunk decides between the readings.

ambiguities.quote: In the caverns of the metals
readings: Literal metals as the place where the Stone is hidden.
'Metals' used in a veiled sense for the subject.
ambiguities.basis: ¶3 stresses deliberately equivocal language; ¶9 says the Water 'gives life to the metals'. The chunk does not define 'metals'.

ambiguities.quote: which contains in its veins the blood of the Pelican
readings: The same as the Fixed Salt, 'the Blood of our Stone' (¶7).
An unexplained image for some vital content of the white Stone.
ambiguities.basis: Both use 'blood' for something within the Stone, but the text never links them.

ambiguities.quote: it is the Sea of the Wise, in which they angle for their mysterious Fish
readings: The Fish is the seed or Sulphur extracted from the body in the First Key.
ambiguities.basis: ¶3 says the First Key extracts 'the seed out of the body' and Hermes' saying is cited as demonstrating that Key, but the Fish is never glossed.

ambiguities.quote: for it is Nature which makes it in a manner incomprehensible to the Artist
readings: In the First Key the Artist only assists Nature, which makes the compound.

In tension with ¶3, where the First Key 'forms the Stone' and the Wise Artist cuts off the Black Dragon's head in the first operation: perhaps Nature makes the compound and the Artist then purifies it.

threads.note: The chapter heading announces six Keys; only the First to Third appear in this chunk, so the Fourth to Sixth should follow.
'the three works' are said to be analogous; the Second and Third Work are mentioned (¶9) but not described here.
The speaker promises to 'enlarge myself more than others have done on this Third Key'; the treatment continues through ¶8–¶9 and likely past this chunk.
'the compound of Nature, whereof I have spoken in the First Key' points back to ¶3.
'The compound of Art is not altogether the same in the Second as in the Third Work' anticipates a later treatment of the Third Work.
The chunk ends mid-thought with 'shines....'; the passage on the water's names continues in the next chunk.
